Existing tools (Diligent, BoardPro) focus on meeting administration (agendas, minutes, action items) — they do NOT provide real-time director duty compliance checking or decision guidance. B2B tier for accounting firms at NZ$199/mo (manage director duty compliance for 10+ director clients).

opportunities.title: NZ Commercial Lease AI Review & Make-Good Protector
opportunities.pain_point: NZ small businesses sign commercial leases without fully understanding make-good obligations, rent review mechanisms, outgoings, assignment clauses, and bond return conditions. Make-good costs routinely surprise tenants at lease end — removal of fit-out, repainting, carpet replacement, and structural reinstatement can cost $20k-$100k+. Commercial lease bonds (2-6 months rent) are frequently disputed, with landlords claiming deductions for 'betterment' (improvements beyond the lease-required standard). Sprintlaw NZ: make-good disputes are the #1 source of bond retention issues. Unlike residential tenancies (which have the Tenancy Tribunal), commercial lease disputes go to arbitration or court — costs quickly exceed the amount in dispute. Most small business owners never get a lawyer to review their lease (typical cost $1k-3k), signing on gut feel about the monthly rent number. Sources: Sprintlaw NZ commercial lease bond analysis; Hesketh Henry 'Make Your Premises Good Again'; Law Association Deed of Lease standard terms; Property Council NZ commercial leasing data.
opportunities.target_audience: NZ SMEs renting commercial premises (~150k businesses with physical premises in retail, hospitality, office, industrial space). Primary buyers: business owners approaching lease renewal, expansion, or first-time lease signers. Secondary: accountants and business advisors advising clients on occupancy costs.
opportunities.proposed_solution: AI commercial lease review & make-good protector: (1) Upload your lease (or key terms) — AI extracts and explains in plain English: rent review mechanism, make-good scope, outgoings structure, assignment/sublease rights, bond amount and return conditions, termination rights, (2) Lease risk score: green/yellow/red for each key clause cluster, (3) Make-good cost estimator: enter fit-out details + lease term + property type — AI estimates likely end-of-lease make-good costs based on NZ market averages and clause wording, (4) Exit readiness passport: start building your exit document package from day one — photos, condition reports, fit-out approvals, maintenance records, (5) Negotiation letter generator: draft requests to reduce bond, narrow make-good scope, clarify return timeline, (6) Bond dispute assistant: if landlord withholds bond, AI generates demand letter citing specific lease clauses, (7) Rent review predictor: based on lease formula + current market rents, forecasts next rent review outcome. Monetise at NZ$49 one-off for a single lease review, NZ$19/mo subscription for ongoing monitoring + make-good passport + rent review alerts. B2B tier for accounting firms at NZ$79/mo (manage lease reviews for 10+ business clients).
opportunities.ringo_role: Build web app with AI lease clause extraction engine (train on NZ commercial lease templates — Law Association Deed of Lease, ADLS forms), make-good cost estimator with NZ construction/cleaning market rates, bond dispute letter templates (NZ law reviewed). Marketing via accounting firm partnerships, Property Council NZ, chambers of commerce, and business advisory networks.
opportunities.neil_role: 1 hr/month for NZ commercial property context and make-good cost reasonableness validation. Neil's network provides beta testers who are small business owners with upcoming lease renewals.
opportunities.the_catch: Commercial lease law is governed by the specific lease wording — AI analysis will be approximate, not definitive. Every lease is different and NZ has no standardised commercial lease (unlike the ADLS residential form). Liability risk if the AI misses a critical clause. Most small businesses only think about their lease when they renew or exit, making ongoing subscription a tough sell. The one-off review model ($49) may be more realistic than monthly subscription. Also, Property Council NZ already offers leasing guidance to members. However, the 'make-good passport' (ongoing document accumulation from day one) is a genuine differentiator that solves the #1 pain point: not having records when the dispute arrives.
opportunities.the_ask: Greenlight = I interview 10 small business owners with upcoming lease renewals about their understanding of make-good obligations and bond terms. If 5/10 can't explain their make-good obligations accurately, the education gap is real. Cost: 3 hours.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue to validation — the commercial lease pain is universal among NZ SMEs with premises, yet no tool exists. The 'make-good passport' (start collecting exit docs from day one) is the wedge. B2B accounting firm channel is the distribution path. Start with the one-off lease review, upsell to ongoing passport.
opportunities.next_action: Interview 10 SME owners about lease terms understanding + assess ADLS/Law Association lease templates for AI parsing + map competitive landscape

opportunities.title: NZ Importer/Exporter Landed Cost & Tariff Intelligence Agent

Most breweries track production and sales in spreadsheets — academic research puts spreadsheet error rates at ~94%. Excise duty rose ~$94M over three years (CPI-indexed). opportunities.target_audience: NZ craft breweries (~200+), distilleries, cider/mead producers — small producers ~10% of the alcohol market; plus the accountants who file for them.

Brewers are under-capitalised and price-sensitive. Accountants already do this for them (channel play or competitor). US vendors (ShipCompliant/Sovos, Ekos) prove the category but don't localise for NZ Customs.
